name: Classical false-position scalar root solver
definition: For a sign-changing bracket (a,b), set x=(af(b)−bf(a))/(f(b)−f(a)); return if f(x)=0, otherwise replace the endpoint sharing its sign with x.
variables: a,b bracket endpoints; f scalar continuous function; interpolation history
assumptions: Continuous real f with sign-changing endpoints; nonzero denominator and bounded iterations.
limitations: One endpoint may remain fixed for many iterations; residual and bracket width need separate stopping rules.
failure_conditions: Invalid bracket, nonfinite values, stagnation or iteration budget exceeded
computation: Provisional secant-intercept formula with bracket update; source and overlap review required.

name: Open inverse quadratic scalar root iteration
definition: For three points x_i with distinct y_i=f(x_i), set x_new=Σ_i x_i Π_(j≠i) (−y_j)/(y_i−y_j); discard the oldest point and repeat unless converged.
variables: a,b bracket endpoints; f scalar continuous function; interpolation history
assumptions: Three distinct finite function values; local smoothness and a simple root for useful convergence.
limitations: No bracket guarantee; close function values can produce unstable extrapolation.
failure_conditions: Coincident function values, nonfinite or divergent iterate, or exhausted budget
computation: Provisional inverse Lagrange interpolation at y=0; check standalone novelty against Brent before admission.
